translations.text: You were proud with feasting and full of wine, you swaggered in your glory, and I was thirsting for the body of God, for the drink of the spirit.
Now you are dumb and deaf, and your joys are worth nothing.

Yet I must, of necessity, seek you out by night, wounded by sins, and then soon turn away from you again at cockcrow, when holy men sing songs of praise to the living God, and go to seek the dwellings which you have assigned to me here,

[?] [would that you had been] there as God wished, yes, even though you were the grimmest of the race of worms, there as God wished, rather than that you ever became a man on earth or should ever receive baptism.
when you must answer for us both on that great day, when the wounds will be revealed to men which sinful men committed long ago in the world,
then afterwards we two must together endure such miseries as you assigned to us here before!"
Then the spirits speak good words, wise and victorious, and in this way they truly greet the body with joy:
"Dearest friend, although worms still greedily attack you, now your spirit has come, beautifully adorned, from my Father's kingdom, wrapped in honours.
You humbled [?] yourself before men and raised me up into eternal joy.
Therefore I shall always long, dearest of men, hard in my mind, because I know that you are in these humiliations, a feast for worms; but God willed that you should ever choose such a loathsome bed.
